sentences.text: Heard learned Senior Advocate Mr.S.Sriranga with learned advocate Smt.Deepika Joshi for the complainant and learned advocate Mr.S.V.Desai for the respondent.

2. The contempt jurisdiction of this Court is invoked in respect of the order dated 11.09.2015 passed by learned Single Judge in Writ Petition No.36132 of 2015 which reads as under,
"Respondent-MUDA not to alienate, encumber or anyway dispose of the immovable property in question until disposal of this petition."
3. The case of the petitioner was inter alia
that she was the owner of the properties situated at Nachanahalli Village, Kasaba Hobli, Mysuru Taluk which were survey Nos.152/A, 153, 154/A, 157/A and 158, having different measurements
. Under the provisions of the Karnataka Urban Development Authority Act, 1987, the said lands came to be acquired for which the Final Notification was issued on 09.03.1998.

3.1 At a subsequent point of time, the Mysuru Urban Development Authority (MUDA) decided to drop the acquisition NC: 2024:KHC:21824-DB proceedings since the complainant and her brothers relinquished the rights in respect of 6 Acres and 11 Guntas of land out of 32 Acres of total acquired land without claiming any compensation.
The Commissioner of the MUDA communicated the said decision to the brother of the complainant, but the Government of Karnataka rejected the proposal.
3.2 The acquisition proceedings continued.
It appears that the award came to be passed by the competent authority in respect of the lands.
However, the compensation awarded was not paid to the complainant nor was remitted to the reference court.
The complainant challenged this acquisition proceedings in the said writ petition in which the above interim order was passed.
3.3 It is the grievance of the petitioner that she was shocked to learn that the land in survey No.157 came to be allotted by MUDA to one Kanaka Guru Peeta.
Despite of the fact that the interim order was operating, one Ramegowda deliberately trespassed on the complainant's abovementioned property bearing survey No.157/A between 04.03.2022 and 09.03.2022.
The request to vacate was not yielded to by the encroachers.
Nothing yielded even after issuance of legal notice.

sentences.text: Upon filing of the contempt petition, a Coordinate Bench of this Court issued notice.
The respondents appeared and filed their compliance report.

In the compliance report, following facts were stated by the respondent,
(i) The record disclosed that site No.216 measuring 15 x 24 mtrs. was allotted in favour of Smt.Radhika S.Kumar as an alternate site on 29.04.2022 and the absolute sale deed was executed on 09.05.2022.

(ii) The record disclosed that site No.217/A measuring 15 x 24 mtrs. was allotted on 29.04.2022 in favour of Shri Basavalingappa as an alternate site which was again sold in favour of Shri M.N.Nandeesh on 29.08.2022.
(iii) The record further disclosed that site No.224 measuring 15 x 24 mtrs. was allotted on 14.07.2003 and the sale deed was executed on 05.11.2003.

(iv) The record further disclosed that site No.220 measuring 15 x 24 mtrs. was allotted on 14.07.2003 to Shri Kameshwar Rao, that is much prior to the interim order passed by this Court in the aforementioned writ petition.
Upon the death of the allottee, the NC: 2024:KHC:21824-DB allotment was transferred to his son Shri K.Sandeep on 04.02.2011 and the absolute sale deed was executed on 23.05.2016.

(v) The execution of the absolute sale deed on 23.05.2016 is a bona fide, inadvertent mistake without noticing the interim order passed by this Court and also for not ascertaining as to whether the site in question is a part and parcel of the lands which are involved in the aforementioned writ petition.

4.1 It was stated that the allotment of site Nos.217/A, 216 on 29.04.2022 as above and the execution of sale deeds was inadvertently done and it was a bona fide mistake without noticing the interim order.
It was stated that the action was not intentional but through oversight for not noticing the fact that the said site is a part of survey No.158 which is subject matter of the pending writ petition.
4.2 It was pointed out that in respect of the acquired land, the Preliminary Notification was issued on 08.01.1992 and Final Notification on 09.03.1998.
It was claimed that the land was vast developing land due to which it was difficult to identify the sites, allotment, records etc.

It was further stated that the Commissioner of MUDA immediately upon noticing the above mistake in allotting and executing the sale deeds in respect of the above three sites, which was unintentional and inadvertent, passed individual orders dated 01.04.2024 cancelling the allotment of the three sites.
Further, the allottees were required to obtain allotment of alternative sites after surrendering the original documents in respect of the earlier allotted sites.
5. Thus, as stated in the compliance affidavit, the Commissioner of MUDA when noticed the mistake, immediately proceeded to rectify it.
It was reiterated that the allotment and execution of the sale deed in respect of the aforesaid three sites was a sheer mistake committed unintentionally.

sentences.text: Not only that, having realized the mistake, the Commissioner passed individual orders on 01.04.2024 cancelling the allotment of the three sites and directing the allottees to obtain allotment of alternative sites by surrendering the original documents.
The factum of cancellation of three sites came to be communicated to the complainant on 01.04.2024 itself.
It was shown that the Commissioner took immediate steps and rectified the mistake by cancelling the wrong allotments done.
The Commissioner took swift steps and took decision to purge the contempt.
There is no reason not to believe that the mistake was bona fide when the allotment was done.
The record was bulky and the site records were large because of which the allotment went unnoticed.
The explanation furnished is both reasonable and plausible.

5.2 When the mistake is found inadvertent and the breach of the direction is also cured by cancelling the allotment of three sites, as stated above, it could not be said that any willful contempt was committed.
The orders of cancelling the allotment of sites are produced at Annexures-R1 to R3 which could be accepted as compliance of the order brought under contempt.
Even if it was breached in the interregnum, it was not an intentional breach to tantamount to contempt.
6. For all the aforesaid reasons, the present contempt is not liable to be entertained.
7. The petition is dismissed.

NC: 2024:KHC:21824-DB While parting, it is provided that in pursuance of the cancellation orders (Annnexures-R1 to R3) after receiving original documents from the allottees, the Mysuru Urban Development Authority shall take necessary steps and measures.

Sd/-
